battle.name: 曹魏與高句麗的戰爭
battle.brief: 正始五年（244）二月，曹叡詔司馬懿、毌丘儉率步騎四萬伐高句麗，渡遼水進逼玄菽、襄平，逼得高句麗遣使請和受封；正始六年再舉五萬大軍深入，卻因糧盡遇雪、士卒飢病而潰退，死者數千。卡面科林斯青銅盔代表重裝步兵與甲騎的頭面防護——全正面開眼，視野最窄，戴盔者只能靠隊形活命。

kit.name: 科林斯青銅盔
kit.history: 全正面開眼的青銅盔。看得見的代價是：戴它的人只能靠隊形活。

countries: 這場戰爭是曹魏在遼東方向對高句麗發動的兩次大規模軍事行動，橫跨正始五年（244）至正始六年（245）冬，歷時近兩個年度。曹魏一方由皇帝曹叡直接下詔，太傅司馬懿與撓平將軍毌丘儉分任中軍與前鋒，率步騎兵團自遼東郡治襄平一線渡遼水向東北推進，後方由幽州、薊城、遼西方向的屯田與漕運供應糧秣，隨軍輜重車隊以牛馬挽曳，逐段搬運給養。高句麗一方是名義上仍奉曹魏正朔的東夷屬國，實則自領部族的王國：都城在丸都（今吉林集安一帶），控制遼河以東、鴨綠江以北的廣大山地與河谷，王下設有邊境諸部，首都與各部城柵以木柵、土壘與冬季結冰的牆垣組成，兵員以本部丁壯為主，少量漢人降附與樂浪舊民亦被編入。雙方實力結構懸殊：曹魏能一次集結數萬大軍與攻城器械，卻受制於遠距離補給；高句麗國土廣而人口疏，無法與魏軍在平原正面決鬥，只能依托山林的遊騎與堅城消耗遠征隊。全役由曹魏的戰略主動開始，以魏軍未能攻滅高句麗、反而折損兵將收場，主要戰線在襄平、玄菽、沃沮、樂浪一線的山地與雪原間展開，即今日遼寧中東部至吉林東南的走廊地帶。
countriesEn: This war covers two large-scale military campaigns launched by Cao Wei against Goguryeo on the Liaodong front, stretching across the fifth and sixth years of Zhengshi (244–245) and lasting close to two full years. The Wei side acted on an imperial edict from Emperor Cao Rui: the Grand Tutor Sima Yi and General Guanqiu Jian, who held the command of Niaoping, were assigned the central army and the vanguard respectively, and they led a force of infantry and cavalry across the Liao River from the commandery seat of Xiangping in Liaodong toward the northeast, while the rear was supplied by the garrisons, farms and sea-borne transport of Youzhou, Ji and western Liaoxi, with baggage carts drawn by oxen and horses carrying provisions forward stage by stage. Goguryeo was nominally a subject state of Cao Wei that still used the Wei calendar, but in practice it governed its own tribes: the capital lay at Wandu, in the area of present-day Ji'an in Jilin, and it held the broad mountain ranges and river valleys east of the Liao River and north of the Yalu. Beneath the king stood frontier tribes and local chiefs, and the capital together with the tribal strongholds was ringed with wooden palisades, earthen ramparts and, in winter, walls of frozen water. The soldiers were drawn mainly from the local adult males, with a few surrendered Han Chinese and former Lelang inhabitants folded into the ranks. The imbalance between the two sides was structural: Cao Wei could concentrate tens of thousands of men and siege engines in a single campaign, yet it was chained to the length of its supply lines; Goguryeo, with a broad country and a thin population, could not meet the Wei army in an open plain and could only wear the expedition down with mounted harassment and stubborn defended towns. The whole war began on the Wei side's strategic initiative and ended with the Wei army failing to destroy Goguryeo and instead losing men and commanders. The main line of operations ran along Xiangping, Xuantu, Wuju and Lelang, through the mountain country and snow fields of what are now central and eastern Liaoning and southeastern Jilin.
people: 人物線上有三組人馬。第一組是曹魏的決策層：皇帝曹叡在正始五年二月下詔東征，屬於主戰的一派，重視結果甚於遠征成本；朝中反對遠出者也曾提出兵遠勞民的顧慮，但詔令既下便不再更改。掌軍者是兩位曹魏中期的柱石。太傅司馬懿統中軍，負責自遼東向東北迂回、策應與警戒糧道，這是他第一次以大軍統帥身份主持對外的大規模用兵，遼東的經驗與戰功為他日後在魏廷的權位累積了資本。撓平將軍毌丘儉是前鋒主將，領主力渡遼水、攻玄菽、進逼襄平，其人治軍嚴整而性剛，第二次遠征深入苦寒失利後一度被免職，隨後復出；他更著名的結局是嘉平元年高平陵之變後被司馬懿夷滅三族。第二組是高句麗的王庭人物：據《資治通鑑》記載，國王為其弟密友所殺，密友一度掌握政權，密友死後其子拔繼位並向曹魏請和，隨後又與魏軍交兵；各部首領與往來使臣的姓名散見於《通鑑》與《三國志》附載的東夷傳，各書所載互有出入，通行說法以密友弒兄奪位、拔繼位受封最為常見。第三組是無名之眾：曹魏一方的重裝步兵與甲騎，高句麗一方的遊騎與弓手；正是這些戴著兜鍪、覆著皮甲的士卒，在遼東山地與風雪之間承受了這場戰爭的實際重量。
peopleEn: Three groups of people stand at the centre of this war. The first is the Wei decision-making circle: Emperor Cao Rui issued the edict for the eastern campaign in the second month of the fifth year of Zhengshi, and belonged to the party that prized results over the cost of distant campaigning; voices in the court had raised the objection that war far from home exhausted the people, but once the edict was issued it was not withdrawn. The men who held the armies were two pillars of mid-period Cao Wei. The Grand Tutor Sima Yi commanded the central army, responsible for turning northeast out of Liaodong, for supporting the vanguard and for guarding the supply road, and this was the first time he led a major foreign campaign in person as commander of a great army; the experience and the credit won in Liaodong added to the capital he would later accumulate in the Wei court. General Guanqiu Jian, who held the command of Niaoping, was the leader of the vanguard: he took the main body across the Liao River, assaulted Xuantu and drove towards Xiangping. He was a man who kept his troops tight but was stubborn in temperament, and after the second expedition failed in the bitter cold he was dismissed from his post for a time before being restored. His far more famous end came in the first year of Jiaping, when after the incident at Gaopingling Sima Yi wiped out his three clans. The second group is the Goguryeo court: according to the Zizhi Tongjian, the king was killed by his younger brother Miyou, who seized power for a time; after Miyou died his son Ba succeeded and sued for peace with Cao Wei, then went back to war with the Wei army. The names of the tribal chiefs and the envoys who came and went are scattered through the Tongjian and through the Dongyi treatise appended to the Records of the Three Kingdoms, and the different books disagree with one another; the most common account has Miyou killing his brother to seize the throne and Ba succeeding him and receiving investiture. The third group is the nameless multitude: the armoured infantry and the armoured horse of Cao Wei, the free riders and the bowmen of Goguryeo. It was these men, in their caps and leather armour, who actually bore the weight of the war between the mountains of Liaodong and the wind and snow.
kits: 卡面這件科林斯青銅盔是公元前七世紀上半葉的希臘工藝，在本場戰爭中當然不曾出現；兵器娘卡牌慣例是以一件可辨識的代表性器物，標示該場戰爭某一部位的裝備類型，這裡標的正是頭面防護。科林斯盔的形制是全覆面青銅殼，只有眼孔、鼻脊與下緣的縫隙可以透光，內襯皮帽以免磨傷頭顱，盔頂留有插冠羽的孔。它的取捨極明確：正面幾乎看不見東西，聽覺與腳步的判斷比視覺重要，於是戴盔者只能靠緊密隊形、旗號與口令和後排的呼喝活命。對照公元244至245年的遼東戰線，兩軍頭面最接近這種全封閉防護的是曹魏的重裝步兵與重騎：兜鍪加頓項乃至金屬面當，札甲、披膊、馬甲鎧構成全身鎧裝，正是三國時代曹魏甲兵重裝化的高峰；高句麗方面則以皮甲、骨甲配尖頂兜鍪或骨盔，少數頭戴面當的骨札裝甲帥。魏軍同期真正大量裝備的遠程兵器是弩與小型擲射器，近身是環首刀與長柄戟，攻城靠雲梯、臨車與衝車，鹿角、拒馬與鐵蒺藜用於阻塞道路；高句麗以短弓、石骨鏃與直刀為主，配木製長矛與皮盾，缺金屬攻城器械。運輸與補給同樣是關鍵：魏軍糧秣自幽州沿海轉運，車隊極長，一旦被遊騎切斷，退路就立刻變成災難。總結而言，頭盔的形制代價——看不見就靠隊形——正是這場戰爭兩邊共同的答案：魏軍靠縱隊與糧道維持，輸在糧道；高句麗靠遊騎與城柵維持，贏在耐心。
kitsEn: The Corinthian helmet on the card is Greek work from the first half of the seventh century before the common era, and it naturally did not appear in this war; the custom of the arms-girl card deck is to use one identifiable artefact to mark the class of equipment belonging to a particular slot in a given war, and the slot marked here is head and face protection. The shape of a Corinthian helmet is a fully enclosing bronze shell, admitting light only through the eye holes, the nasal ridge and the gap at the lower edge, with a leather liner inside to keep the metal from grinding the skull, and a hole in the crown for a crest or plume. Its bargain is perfectly explicit: almost nothing can be seen straight ahead, so hearing and the reading of footsteps matter more than sight, and the man wearing it can only stay alive through tight formation, through flags and calls, and through the shouts of the rank behind. Set against the Liaodong front of 244–245, the closest thing to such a fully closed protection on either side was the armoured infantry and heavy horse of Cao Wei: a cap with a neck guard and even a metal face plate, with lamellar armour, shoulder guards and horse armour making up a full suit, the high point of the heavier and heavier armoured cavalry of Cao Wei in the Three Kingdoms period. Goguryeo, by contrast, used leather and bone armour with pointed caps or bone helmets, and only a very few commanders wore face plates over bone-and-lamellar harness. The long-range weapons Cao Wei really fielded in quantity were the crossbow and small artillery pieces; close combat was fought with ring-pommel sabres and long halberds; siege was carried by scaling ladders, siege towers and battering rams, with cheval-de-frise, spiked barriers and iron caltrops used to block the roads. Goguryeo fought with short bows, stone and bone arrowheads and straight swords, with wooden spears and hide shields, and possessed no metal siege engines. Transport and supply were just as decisive: the Wei grain and provisions came up the coast from Youzhou in very long wagon columns, and once the free riders cut that road, the line of retreat turned into a disaster at once. In the end the bargain of the helmet — if you cannot see, you depend on formation — is the common answer of both sides in this war: the Wei army held together through marching columns and supply roads and lost on the supply road; Goguryeo held together through its riders and its fortified towns and won on patience.
tactics: 曹魏的戰法是分進合擊。正始五年二月詔下後，太傅司馬懿與撓平將軍毌丘儉分兵：主力由毌丘儉領，渡遼水向東北的玄菽方向搜索，司馬懿率中軍為第二路，兩軍以旌旗鼓噪互相策應，目標是趁高句麗王庭內亂、諸部據城自守之際，尋找可以一舉奪取的城柵與名分。攻城用的是曹魏最成熟的一套：弩手列陣前壓，壓制城頭，雲梯、臨車與衝車同時靠城，工兵拆毀門樓與木柵；破城之後並不長久停留，而是分選人口、糧秣與牲口，遷回內地，再分兵掃蕩周邊城邑。正始六年的第二次遠征戰法幾乎照搬，但目標由受降變成滅國：軍隊越過玄菽，深入沃沮與丸都方向的山地，縱隊拉得更長，側翼不得不分出大量騎兵護衛，結果不但沒有了明確的攻城目標，反而把整支大軍變成一條向東北延伸、缺乏補給的長線。撤退的安排是這一役最要命的環節：糧道已被切斷，連日雨雪，士卒飢病，隊伍必須在飢寒中回望來路，而高句麗的遊騎正沿山道與林緣不斷貼近騷擾，逼著魏軍在士氣與體力崩潰的狀態下作戰，於是退卻變成潰退，士卒死者數千。相對地，高句麗的戰法是不求一決、專務纏磨：不與魏軍在平原硬碰，而以小股騎兵分割、遮斷糧道，把魏軍拖進自己的地盤；城守則以木柵、土壘與冬季結冰的牆垣延緩魏軍攻勢，待其銳氣與糧秣耗盡再行反擊。雙方的勝負手其實是同一件事：誰先耗盡對方的時間。
tacticsEn: The Wei method was to advance in separate columns and strike together. After the edict of the second month of the fifth year of Zhengshi, the Grand Tutor Sima Yi and General Guanqiu Jian split their forces: the main body under Guanqiu Jian crossed the Liao River and searched northeastward around Xuantu, while Sima Yi led the central army as a second column, the two columns supporting each other by flags and drums, the object being to seize, while the Goguryeo court was in confusion and the tribes were holding their own towns, some walled place and some claim to legitimacy that could be taken in a single stroke. Besieging followed the most mature Wei method: crossbowmen formed up in front to pin the wall, scaling ladders, siege towers and battering rams came up together, and engineers pulled down gate towers and palisades; after a town fell the army did not linger but sorted the people, the grain and the livestock out, moved them inland, and then sent columns to clear the neighbouring settlements. The second expedition of the sixth year of Zhengshi copied this method almost exactly, but its object had changed from receiving a surrender to destroying the state: the army passed Xuantu and pushed deep into the mountains towards Wuju and Wandu, the marching column grew longer, and large numbers of horsemen had to be detached to guard the flanks; instead of a clear siege target it now had a great army stretched into a long, poorly supplied line running northeast. The handling of the retreat was the most fatal part of the campaign: the supply road had been cut, rain and snow continued day after day, the men were hungry and sick, and the column had to look back along its own track in want of food and warmth, while Goguryeo's free riders kept closing in along the mountain tracks and the edge of the forest, forcing the Wei army to fight while its morale and its strength were collapsing, so that a withdrawal turned into a rout and several thousand men were lost. Goguryeo's method, by contrast, was to seek no decisive battle and to wear its opponent down: it would not meet the Wei army in the open plain, but would cut the army into fragments with small bodies of horse, sever the supply road, and drag the Wei army deep into its own country; for the defence of towns it relied on wooden palisades, earthen ramparts and, in winter, walls of frozen water, to slow the Wei assault and to strike back once the attacker's edge and supplies were spent. The deciding factor was in fact the same thing for both sides: who would exhaust the other one's time first.
data: 可核對的數字有限，而且多出自《資治通鑑》卷八十二與《三國志·毌丘儉傳》。第一次遠征，通鑑記步騎四萬人，可視為曹魏在遼東方向一次性投入的極限兵力；第二次遠征另記步騎五萬人，兩次相加近九萬人，在三國時代的東線是極大的集中。戰役橫跨兩個年度：正始五年二月出師，五月前後打到玄菽與襄平一線；正始六年再度出兵，據記載深入之後遇雨雪四十餘日、糧盡、士卒飢病，撤退時士卒死者數千。距離與地理尺度方面：襄平（今遼寧遼陽）至玄菽（今遼寧撫順一帶）約二百餘里，再往東北到沃沮、接近丸都（今吉林集安一帶）又是數百里；退軍要走完這條線，而魏軍的糧秣車隊要從幽州、遼西沿海運到襄平再向前接應，單程就是數百里。人口與物資的取用也有記載：曹魏在先後平定樂浪、玄菽的戰事中遷樂浪、玄菽、帶方等郡民數萬口內屬，諸郡遂廢；244年遠征破城之後同樣有分選人口、遷往內地的動作，但數量因記載殘缺而不詳。損失方面，傳世記載最確定的一句是撤退途中士卒死者數千，此外魏廷追究敗退之責、毌丘儉一度被免職，也可從側面說明此役的代價。相對地，高句麗方面的具體傷亡與損耗數字幾乎沒有留下，只能確定其在玄菽、襄平方向一度失去外城與屏障，其內部因王位更替而分裂的力量則在戰後迅速重新整合。
dataEn: The verifiable figures are few, and most come from the eighty-second chapter of the Comprehensive Mirror and from the biography of Guanqiu Jian in the Records of the Three Kingdoms. For the first expedition the Mirror records forty thousand foot and horse, which may be taken as the limit Cao Wei was able to commit on the Liaodong front in a single campaign; the second expedition records fifty thousand foot and horse, and the two together come close to ninety thousand men, an enormous concentration for the eastern front in the Three Kingdoms period. The war straddled two years: the army set out in the second month of the fifth year of Zhengshi and reached the Xuantu and Xiangping line around the fifth month; in the sixth year it marched out again, and the accounts say that after pushing deep it met more than forty days of rain and snow, ran out of food, and left the men hungry and sick, with several thousand dead on the retreat. As for distance and the scale of the ground: from Xiangping, in present-day Liaoyang in Liaoning, to Xuantu, in the Fushun area of the same province, is rather more than two hundred li, and from there northeast to Wuju and close to Wandu, in the Ji'an area of present-day Jilin, is several hundred li more; the retreat had to retrace that whole line, while the Wei baggage train carried grain and provisions from the coast of Youzhou and western Liaoxi up to Xiangping and onward to meet the army, a single leg of it running for several hundred li. There is also a record of the taking of people and goods: when Cao Wei had earlier broken Lelang and Xuantu it moved several tens of thousands of the inhabitants of Lelang, Xuantu and Bianfang inland and the commanderies were abolished; after the towns fell in the 244 campaign there was the same sorting of captives and removal of people inland, but the numbers are lost because the records are fragmentary. On losses, the single most certain sentence in the transmitted text is that several thousand soldiers died on the retreat; the Wei court's decision to hold the responsible commanders accountable and the temporary dismissal of Guanqiu Jian also show the price of the campaign from the side. By contrast, almost no figures survive for Goguryeo's own casualties and material loss; what can be established is that it lost its outer works and its screen around Xuantu and Xiangping for a time, while the forces split by the change of kingship were quickly reunited after the war.
cause: 遠征的第一層原因是曹魏自己的目標未竟。曹叡在景初至正始年間先後平定樂浪與玄菽，遷其民內屬，把樂浪、帶方、玄菽三郡廢掉，表面上把高句麗壓回山東；然而被廢的郡土並沒有真正歸於曹魏的直接管轄，而是落入高句麗與其附屬部族的實際控制之中，遼東與高句麗之間自此只剩下一層脆弱的緩衝。曹魏廷在這個缺口上並不安寧：玄菽一失，遼東郡治襄平就直接暴露在東北方向。第二層原因是高句麗內部的王位變亂。據《資治通鑑》記載，高句麗國王為其弟密友所殺，密友奪權，諸部據城自守，而內部又有人向曹魏請降求援；這在兵家看來是難得的以亂為師的機會，詔令東征便以救其國君、誅其亂臣的名義發出。第三層原因是曹魏對東北方的戰略需求：只要把樂浪故地與玄菽一線重新釘在曹魏的郡縣框架上，魏廷就能同時壓住遼東，堵住高句麗與東吳之間的聯繫；反之若放棄，高句麗便會在魏、吳相持的年月裡坐大。第四層原因是時間窗口。曹叡在位時的曹魏尚能以國家力量驅動一次數萬人的遠征，司馬懿剛在遼東平定公孫氏不久，軍心與名將資源都還在手上；一旦內廷的權力競逐加劇、將領之間互相猜忌，這樣的機會便不會再有。於是對魏廷而言，趁亂一舉與逼和而後安之間，只能選前者。
causeEn: The first layer of cause is that Cao Wei's own objective remained unfinished. Between the Jingshu and Zhengshi eras Emperor Cao Rui broke Lelang and Xuantu in turn, moved their inhabitants inland and abolished the commanderies of Lelang, Bianfang and Xuantu, which on the face of it pressed Goguryeo back into the mountains; yet the soil of the abolished commanderies did not really pass under direct Wei administration, but fell into the actual control of Goguryeo and its dependent tribes, and from that moment only a fragile buffer separated Liaodong from Goguryeo. The Wei court was not at ease about this gap: once Xuantu was lost, the Liaodong commandery seat at Xiangping lay directly exposed to the northeast. The second layer of cause is the change of kingship inside Goguryeo. According to the Comprehensive Mirror the Goguryeo king was killed by his younger brother Miyou, Miyou seized power, the tribes held their own towns, and yet someone inside Goguryeo sued Cao Wei for help; to a strategist this was a rare chance to profit from an enemy's confusion, and the edict went out in the name of restoring the rightful king and punishing the usurper. The third layer is Cao Wei's strategic need in the northeast: if the old Lelang lands and the Xuantu line could be nailed back into the Wei framework of commanderies and counties, the court could simultaneously pin down Liaodong and cut Goguryeo off from contacts with Eastern Wu; if it let the matter go, Goguryeo would grow strong in the years when Wei and Wu wore each other down. The fourth layer is the window of opportunity. While Cao Rui lived, Cao Wei could still drive a campaign of tens of thousands of men with the whole strength of the state, and Sima Yi had only just settled the Gongsun clan in Liaodong, so the morale of the army and the resources of famous generals were still to hand; once the rivalry inside the palace hardened and the generals began to suspect one another, such a chance would not come again. Between striking now while the enemy was in confusion and forcing a peace first and then settling down, the Wei court could only choose the former.
impact: 這場戰爭的直接結果是曹魏東北戰略的轉向。兩次遠征都沒有把高句麗收進郡縣體系，魏廷自此放棄武力統一遼東以東，改用羈縻與冊封：承認高句麗王的地位，以名義上的臣屬換取邊境安寧，把注意力轉回西線的蜀漢與關東曹爽、司馬懿之間的權力競逐。對高句麗而言，這是因敗而興的典型：曹魏的退兵沒有削弱它，反而讓它得以整合內部、填補因王位更替而出現的裂縫，並穩步接管原屬樂浪、帶方、玄菽的土地，把勢力範圍從鴨綠江以北擴展到遼河下游一線，丸都與襄平之間的山地走廊進入了它的實際控制。它由此成為三國時代東北唯一的強權，在曹、蜀、吳三方角力中保持相對超然的位置，甚至在魏、吳交鋒時得到額外的活動空間。更長遠地看，這一役留下的形勢在數百年後仍有回聲：高句麗在魏晉之際坐大，兩晉與北朝多次嘗試用兵而未能扭轉，最終變成隋朝必須面對的心腹大患，隋軍在598年以後屢次大舉東征，把糧食運到燕、薊、遼東一線，其消耗正是從這段歷史累積而成。對司馬懿個人而言，這是他第一次以大軍統帥身份主持的對外大規模戰役，遼東的經驗、與高句麗周旋的實戰、對東北地理的理解，都成為他在魏廷權力競逐中不可替代的資本，也塑造了他日後對遼東威而不怒、以撫為主的處置風格；對毌丘儉而言，這是仕途上的一次重挫，也是他與司馬懿同在一條戰線上卻結局迥異的起點。
impactEn: The direct result of this war was a turn in Cao Wei's strategy in the northeast. Neither expedition brought Goguryeo into the framework of commanderies and counties, and the court gave up on winning the lands east of Liaodong by force, switching instead to control by investiture: it recognised the position of the Goguryeo king, exchanging a nominal state of subjection for quiet on the frontier, and turned its attention back to Shu Han in the west and to the rivalry between Cao Shao and Sima Yi in the east of the realm. For Goguryeo this was a classic case of growing strong out of a defeat: the Wei withdrawal did not weaken it, it allowed the kingdom to pull its own parts together, to fill the cracks opened by the change of kingship, and to take over steadily the lands that had belonged to Lelang, Bianfang and Xuantu, extending the sphere of control from north of the Yalu down to the lower Liao, and bringing the mountain corridor between Wandu and Xiangping under its actual administration. It thus became the single strong power in the northeast of the Three Kingdoms, holding a relatively detached position amid the three-way contest between Wei, Shu and Wu, and even gaining extra room to manoeuvre when Wei and Wu collided. Looking further ahead, the shape left by this war still echoed centuries later: Goguryeo grew strong across the Wei-Jin transition, the two Jin courts and the northern dynasties tried arms against it without success, and it ended up as the great internal adversary that the Sui had to face, with the Sui army mounting repeated great eastern campaigns after 598 and hauling grain toward Yan, Ji and the Liaodong line, a cost accumulated precisely out of this stretch of history. For Sima Yi personally, this was the first major foreign war he led as commander of a great army; the experience of Liaodong, the hard fighting against Goguryeo and the grasp of the northeastern geography all became capital he could not do without in the struggle for power inside the Wei court, and they shaped the style with which he would later handle Liaodong, stern but not wrathful, persuasion first. For Guanqiu Jian it was a serious blow to his career, and the beginning of a story in which he and Sima Yi stood on the same front line and met utterly different ends.
result: 結局是雙方都沒有得到想要的東西。曹魏以兩次近九萬人次的遠征，換來一個仍然獨立的東北鄰國：第一役在混亂中得手，攻入玄菽、逼近襄平，逼得高句麗方面遣使請和、接受魏廷冊封，可謂不戰而得其名；到了第二役，曹軍深入至玄菽以北的雪原，糧道被遊騎切斷，連日雨雪，士卒飢病，撤退途中被追擊，死者數千，最終原路退回。魏廷追究敗退之責，毌丘儉一度被免職，但曹魏沒有再組織第三次遠征，遼東以東的局勢就此定型：高句麗保持自主，佔有遼東大部與舊樂浪、帶方故地，魏與之維持數十年表面上的君臣關係，直到西晉咸寧元年（277）再起東征、仍無功而還，才徹底斷了以武力解決東北的念頭。從兵器與編制的角度回看，這一役也留下兩個教訓：其一，遠征的成敗不由攻城技術決定，而由補給線決定，四萬、五萬大軍的鋒頭在遼東消耗不盡，真正要命的是那條從幽州海岸延伸到玄菽的糧道；其二，頭面全封閉的防護只在隊形完整時有效——科林斯青銅盔的設計前提是密集縱隊與旗號傳令，一旦隊形被飢寒與追擊打散，看不見的代價就會立刻變成看不清方向的潰散。曹魏的甲兵輸在這裏，高句麗的遊騎贏在這裏，兩千七百年前的東北戰線，結論並不複雜。
resultEn: In the end neither side got what it wanted. Cao Wei spent two expeditions of close to ninety thousand men and received in exchange an independent neighbour in the northeast. The first campaign succeeded amid the confusion: the army entered Xuantu and pressed towards Xiangping, forcing Goguryeo to send envoys to ask for peace and to accept Wei investiture, so that it gained a name without a fight. In the second, the Cao army pushed north of Xuantu into the snow country, its supply road was cut by free riders, rain and snow continued day after day, the men were hungry and sick, and being pursued on the way back several thousand were lost, so that the army eventually retreated by the road it had come. The court held the commanders accountable for the failure and Guanqiu Jian was dismissed for a time, but Cao Wei never organised a third expedition, and the situation east of Liaodong was settled: Goguryeo kept its independence, held the greater part of Liaodong together with the old lands of Lelang and Bianfang, and Wei and Goguryeo kept up a nominal lord-and-vassal relationship for several decades, until the Jin court in the first year of Xianning (277) launched another eastern campaign and also returned with nothing, finally giving up the thought of solving the northeast by arms. Seen from the standpoint of weapons and organisation, the war left two lessons. First, the success or failure of a distant campaign is not decided by siegecraft but by the supply line: the edge of an army of forty or fifty thousand cannot be spent in Liaodong, and what really killed it was the grain road running from the coast of Youzhou all the way to Xuantu. Second, fully closed protection of the head and face works only while the formation holds together. The Corinthian helmet presupposes a dense column and orders passed by flag; once the formation is broken by hunger, cold and pursuit, the price of not seeing turns at once into a rout in which direction cannot be made out. The armoured men of Cao Wei lost on that account, and the free riders of Goguryeo won on it. On a front in the northeast twenty-seven hundred years ago, the conclusion is not a complicated one.
